records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics
records.tldr: These methods measure proteins or selected signals derived from them. Some also measure chemical modifications, which need to be interpreted separately from protein amount.
records.summary: Mass-spectrometry and antibody-based methods measure different protein-derived signals under defined workflows. A primary yeast study measured protein expression alongside phosphorylation and showed why a changed phosphopeptide signal can reflect protein abundance as well as phosphorylation. That methodological result is not a validated cancer-treatment rule. Targeted plasma-protein assays likewise require evidence about recovery, calibration and quantitative range. A protein measurement, modification-site signal, functional pathway dependence and prediction of treatment benefit are distinct claims. Beausoleil and colleagues introduced the Ascore, a probability-based score for how likely a phosphorylation site is correctly localised from site-determining ions in tandem mass spectra, alongside a target-decoy measure of dataset error (2006). In yeast, 25 per cent of seemingly differential phosphopeptides were attributable to changes in protein expression once phosphopeptide ratios were calibrated by protein levels (Wu and colleagues, 2011). In human ovarian tumour and breast cancer xenograft tissue collected without vascular interruption, rapid phosphorylation changes were seen in up to 24 per cent of the phosphoproteome after defined ischaemic intervals, while the global proteome and most of more than 25,000 quantified phosphosites were unchanged after 60 minutes; phosphopeptides in that study were enriched by immobilised metal (Fe3+) affinity chromatography before analysis (Mertins and colleagues, 2014).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). Kinases add phosphate and phosphatases remove it, as the existing phosphorylation record states, and a larger phosphopeptide signal is not a universal sign of greater activity. Enrichment changes what is recovered, so a phosphopeptide sample is not an unbiased count of all proteins. Site localisation is separate from peptide identification and carries its own confidence. A phosphopeptide intensity reflects the source-protein amount, the modified fraction and recovery, so intensity or fold change is not occupancy. A set of supported sites can inform a pathway hypothesis; it does not measure the pathway's rate, prove dependence or show benefit from a drug, and a kinase inferred from a pattern is not measured causality.

Fictional worked example with independent arithmetic. Parent-protein signal rises from 100 to 200 and phosphopeptide signal from 20 to 40, each on its own assay scale: 200 / 100 = 2 and 40 / 20 = 2, so the protein-adjusted relative change is 2 / 2 = 1. The raw 20 / 100 = 0.2 is not the fraction of protein molecules carrying the site, because recovery and response factors differ between the assays, and no activation or kinase-causality conclusion follows. A twofold phosphopeptide rise with a twofold parent-protein rise therefore does not show doubled activation.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Measures and method: enriched phosphorylated peptides, identified sites and quantitative comparisons. Input and tissue cost: a protein extract with recorded collection and preservation; preparation consumes material, and enrichment may need more input than the companion total-protein assay. Output and units: phosphopeptide or site identifiers, localisation scores and relative intensities or ratios, with occupancy percentages only when specifically supported. Thresholds: separate identification error controls, localisation criteria and quantitative limits for the exact workflow. Failure modes: handling-induced change, incomplete recovery, ambiguous sites, low signal and unmeasured parent-protein change. Limits: no automatic activation, enzyme-of-origin, dependency or drug-benefit conclusion. Validation context: check reproducibility, timing controls and site-specific evidence.
records.principle: Measure protein-derived peptide or antibody signals, retaining assay specificity, preparation, calibration and the distinction between protein amount and modification state.
strengths: Measures protein-derived abundance and modification signals

records.name: Imaging mass cytometry
records.tldr: A way to stain a tumour slice for dozens of proteins at once using metal-tagged antibodies read by a mass spectrometer, giving a detailed map of which cells are where.
records.summary: The original imaging mass cytometry method combined metal-tagged antibodies with laser ablation and mass cytometry to map marker signals in tumor sections. Multiplexed ion beam imaging is a related approach that uses secondary ion mass spectrometry; the acquisition methods are distinct. Assigning tissue signals to individual cells also requires image analysis. Marker selection, antibody performance and segmentation affect what a reported cell profile means; a spatial association does not by itself establish a cellular mechanism or treatment response. The original imaging mass cytometry paper coupled immunohistochemical and immunocytochemical staining with high-resolution laser ablation to CyTOF mass cytometry, imaging 32 proteins and modifications at subcellular resolution in human breast cancer samples, with more than 100 markers possible given further isotopes; mass cytometry had previously been applied only to cell suspensions (Giesen and colleagues, 2014). Spillover between channels is reduced compared with dye-based flow cytometry but still exists, and a bead-based compensation workflow was developed to estimate and correct it in suspension and imaging mass cytometry, reducing the risk of reporting cell phenotype artefacts (Chevrier and colleagues, 2018).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The antibody panel selects what can be measured, so imaging mass cytometry is not untargeted proteomics. Laser ablation removes the sampled material, so the scanned region is consumed. Spatial proximity between marker-defined cells is a measured arrangement, not functional interaction, killing or patient benefit. Suspension mass cytometry shares the detection principle but loses the original arrangement.

Fictional worked example. A panel reports a rare double-positive cell population while one marker is extremely bright in a neighbouring mass channel. Before calling a new cell state, inspect channel interference and staining controls and overlay the cell boundaries, because spillover or a merged boundary can create apparent coexpression; even a corrected pattern still needs biological interpretation.

Figure reading (toy grid, light and dark renders agree): a stained section is sampled address by address, the address x2,y1 is recorded and material is removed; the channels for marker A (blue) and marker B (rose) are rebuilt on one grid, with the outlined tile at the same x2,y1 address in both; estimated cell borders need checking; and suspension cells lose this arrangement. Only selected markers are shown and nothing guarantees segmentation.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Input and tissue cost: a compatible tissue section and a validated panel; ablation consumes the scanned region, and field choice and section area limit sampling. Output and units: metal-signal images, per-pixel or per-cell channel values, cell counts, densities per square millimetre and distances in micrometres; signals are not automatically absolute molecule counts. Controls: antibody validation and titration, positive and negative material, interference controls, instrument checks and boundary overlays. Thresholds: explicit marker, phenotype and spatial rules, with no universal immune-response cutoff. Failure modes: channel interference, weak staining, acquisition artefacts, unrepresentative fields, wrong boundaries and inconsistent analysis batches. Cannot tell you: unmeasured proteins, living-cell dynamics, antigen specificity, killing or benefit. Validation context: the panel and pipeline need technical validation.
records.principle: Imaging mass cytometry reads laser-ablated metal-tagged antibody signals from tissue; related ion-beam methods use a distinct acquisition approach.
strengths: Multiple markers localized on one tissue section
Supports cell profiling when staining and segmentation are validated
limitations: Slow acquisition and small fields of view

records.name: Neoantigen
records.tldr: An immune-recognition target arising from a sequence change in a tumor. Sequencing can suggest candidates, while display and recognition need their own evidence.
records.summary: Tumor sequencing can nominate altered protein sequences, and prediction methods can prioritize candidate peptides. Natural presentation and immune recognition are separate questions. A primary melanoma study recovered mutated HLA-associated peptides from native tumor material and tested selected peptides with immune assays. A consortium comparison likewise separated prediction features from measured immune interactions. A tumor-associated sequence alteration alone does not establish presentation, recognition, treatment benefit or a guarantee of healthy-tissue safety.

notes: Evidence for a candidate climbs through separate levels: a sampled tumour-specific alteration (is the altered message expressed?), a matched binding prediction (is it naturally processed and displayed?), a recovered HLA-associated peptide (which cells supplied it, and does a receptor recognise it?) and a controlled response to naturally presenting tumour (healthy-tissue specificity and patient benefit remain open). Altered splicing as well as substitutions, insertions, deletions and rearrangements can create candidate sequences, and not every unusual transcript is tumour-exclusive. Different HLA alleles present different fragments of one altered sequence, so one alteration can yield several candidates or none useful. Wells et al. (Cell 2020, PMID 33038342) tested 608 predicted epitopes for patient-matched T-cell binding; Litchfield et al. (Nature Communications 2020, PMID 32733040) linked frameshift mutations that escape nonsense-mediated decay to checkpoint outcomes in melanoma cohorts. Their performance figures do not transfer to other models, cancers or vaccines.

records.name: Immune measurements and product evidence
records.tldr: Each immune test or product-quality check answers a particular question. Connecting those questions helps explain how a proposed treatment moves from molecular measurements to evidence in people.
records.summary: This reading map links immune-assay readouts, antigen evidence, specimen preparation, RNA design, recognition modules and product quality. It is a set of evidence questions, not a required experimental sequence. Receptor binding, cytokine release, cell killing, lot potency and clinical benefit are different observations. A useful explanation names the sample, assay, model and comparison that support the claim, including the steps that remain untested.

records.name: ELISpot secretion assays
records.tldr: This test records spots where sampled cells release a chosen substance. A spot count describes secretion under the test conditions; other assays address recognition or killing.
records.summary: The original enzyme-linked immunospot method counted antibody-secreting cells; cytokine versions are used to examine stimulated immune-cell responses. Cancer Vaccine Consortium proficiency panels showed that sample handling, protocol choices and plate reading affected results. A result needs the measured molecule, stimulation, cell input, background and reporting rule. A positive secretion response alone does not show that the sampled cells recognize or kill an unmodified tumor.

records.name: Intracellular cytokine staining
records.tldr: This test measures signaling proteins retained inside stimulated cells and identifies which stained cell groups produced them. The result describes a response in the assay.
records.summary: An original multiparameter flow-cytometry study detected intracellular cytokine accumulation after antigen stimulation and measured several cytokines in individual cells. That study concerned viral responses, not cancer-treatment prediction. The stimulated material, measured cytokines, cell groups and analysis gates define the result. Cytokine production is distinct from direct measurement of target-cell death, and assay validation does not by itself establish clinical benefit.

records.name: Peptide-HLA multimer staining
records.tldr: This test labels cells whose receptors bind a particular displayed peptide under the assay conditions. It helps identify a binding population that can then be studied for function.
records.summary: The original peptide-MHC tetramer study made soluble multimeric peptide-display complexes to identify antigen-specific T cells. Binding correlated with cytotoxicity in the tested systems, but those observations are different measurements. The chosen peptide and HLA molecule define which interaction is tested. Detecting multimer-binding cells does not by itself establish natural display of that peptide by a tumor, successful target-cell killing or a clinical treatment effect.

records.name: Immune-cell cytotoxicity assays
records.tldr: These experiments measure whether immune cells cause death of specified target cells. The target cells, comparison conditions and timing are part of the result.
records.summary: A primary flow-cytometry method distinguished labeled target cells from immune effector cells and measured target death while characterizing the effector population. The study examined how timing and the effector-to-target ratio affected the assay. Degranulation markers provide a related functional readout, but they measure a step preceding cytolysis. Killing of a laboratory target does not establish recognition of every tumor cell or benefit in the person receiving a treatment.

records.name: T-cell receptor repertoire sequencing
records.tldr: Receptor sequencing records the immune-receptor sequences sampled from a population of cells. It can track which sequences are present and how their measured abundance changes.
records.summary: An original sequencing study quantified rearranged T-cell receptor beta-chain sequences to examine repertoire diversity. A beta-chain repertoire is a sampled molecular measurement, not a complete map of paired receptors or the antigens they recognize. The specimen, sequencing method and definition of a clonotype belong with the result. Following a sequence over time is distinct from demonstrating its antigen specificity or the function of the cells that carry it.

records.name: T-cell receptor repertoire diversity and clonality
records.tldr: Repertoire measures describe how many receptor identities are sampled and how unevenly they are represented. A dominant sequence does not tell us what its cells recognize.
records.summary: Repertoire sequencing can describe richness and the distribution of sampled receptor sequences. Those summaries depend on the sampled population and the way receptor identities and counts are defined; the original sequencing study found diversity estimates that differed from earlier methods. A repertoire dominated by a clone is a distributional observation. It is distinct from proving tumor specificity, a malignant clone or successful tumor killing, each of which needs additional evidence.

notes: The repertoire is a distribution of receptor identities and abundances in a stated population and time. A clone is a cellular lineage; a clonotype is an operational sequence grouping. Single-chain labels and paired identities have different resolution. V(D)J assembly and thymic selection contribute diversity, while expansion changes abundance; diversity and total T-cell count are different quantities.

Blood, tumour and lymph nodes sample overlapping but different populations. Infection, therapy, age and movement can change a sample; absence from one tube may reflect sampling or detection rather than whole-body absence. A pretreatment blood sample is not a complete stored repertoire. Lower measured diversity after infection may reflect a vigorous response and does not establish cancer specificity, vaccine causation or uniformly worse immunity.

Fictional matched receptor samples contain 10 clonotype A cells among 1,000 T cells (1%) and 10 among 100 (10%). The sampled count remains 10; the changed denominator drives the larger fraction. Absolute expansion requires comparable sampling and calibrated counts, and neither frequency identifies antigen. State sampling depth, chain definition, compartment, method and timing.

records.name: Peripheral blood mononuclear cell specimens
records.tldr: This blood-cell preparation contains lymphocytes and monocytes used in many immune tests. Collection and handling affect which cells and responses can be measured.
records.summary: The National Library of Medicine distinguishes mononuclear leukocytes from granulocytes and from monocytes alone. A primary study of immune monitoring in HIV vaccine research found that processing and cryopreservation conditions affected cell recovery, viability and measured antigen responses. Those were assay findings, not a validated cancer-treatment predictor. A blood preparation also samples a different compartment from a tumor biopsy; the specimen and handling conditions belong with its interpretation.

records.name: Peptide binding, presentation and immune recognition
records.tldr: A peptide can bind a display molecule, be displayed by a cell, or be recognized by an immune receptor. These are different questions that require different evidence.
records.summary: Binding prediction estimates one part of antigen selection. Immunopeptidomics examines peptides recovered with HLA molecules, while immune assays investigate receptor binding and functional responses. A primary melanoma study directly identified naturally presented mutated peptides and separately tested their immunogenicity. A consortium study likewise evaluated prediction against measured immune interactions. A candidate supported at one stage should retain that evidence level rather than being described as a demonstrated therapeutic target.

Evidence maps to claims: a binding prediction supports a model estimate for one exact peptide and allele (Reynisson et al., 2020, PMID 32406916); measured binding supports binding under that assay; immunopeptidomics supports association with the recovered preparation (Purcell et al., 2019, PMID 31092913), not guaranteed cancer-cell origin, surface location or complete recovery; peptide-HLA multimer staining shows cells binding a defined reagent (Altman et al., 1996, PMID 8810254), not affinity or killing; only a controlled response to naturally presenting target cells supports recognition or the measured function. Supplied-peptide stimulation can bypass processing, and secretion and target-cell death are different outputs.

records.name: Immunopeptidome
records.tldr: The immunopeptidome is the collection of peptides associated with immune display molecules in a particular biological setting. A measurement recovers a view of that collection through a defined assay.
records.summary: An immunopeptidome concerns displayed peptide ligands, rather than every protein or RNA message in a sample. Direct analysis of native melanoma tissue identified HLA-associated peptides, including some containing tumor mutations. What is recovered depends on the tissue and analytical workflow. The observed collection should retain its sample and method, and identifying a displayed peptide remains distinct from showing an immune response to it.

notes: The immunopeptidome is a biological repertoire in a defined cell population and context; an immunopeptidomics list is a method-dependent subset recovered and identified from a sample. Class I and class II repertoires are separate, and a protein can be abundant while a derived peptide is poorly generated, loaded or retained. Inflammatory signals changed peptide patterns in cancer cell lines (Chong et al., 2018, ovarian cancer cells and interferon gamma, PMID 29242379; Javitt et al., 2019, lung cancer cells and TNF-alpha and interferon gamma acting through HLA-B, PMID 30833945), which shows context-dependent remodelling and not that inflammation adds useful targets. Whole-lysate capture can recover intracellular as well as surface complexes, mixed tissue adds cancer, immune and stromal sources, relative instrument intensity is not surface copies per cell, and a reported sequence can be misassigned (Wilhelm et al., 2021, PMID 34099720). Method B identifying 1,200 peptides against method A's 800 (fictional) shows no biological difference. Sarkizova et al. (2020) gives allele-dependent repertoires from mono-allelic lines.

records.name: Immunopeptidomics
records.tldr: This laboratory approach identifies peptides recovered with immune display molecules. It supplies evidence about peptide presentation in the material that was analyzed.
records.summary: A primary melanoma study used mass spectrometry to identify HLA-associated peptides from native tumor tissue and then evaluated selected mutated peptides with immune assays. This is stronger evidence of natural presentation in the sampled material than a binding prediction alone. The analytical observation still has a defined specimen and workflow. It does not automatically establish the abundance of a ligand on every cancer cell, receptor recognition or a treatment effect. A published protocol isolates MHC-peptide complexes by immunoaffinity capture, dissociates the peptides by acid denaturation, fractionates them by HPLC and identifies them by nano-UPLC tandem mass spectrometry, from cell lines and tissues (Purcell and colleagues, 2019). Capture starts from mild-detergent solubilised lysates (Chong and colleagues, 2018; Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020 immunoprecipitated HLA from soluble lysates), so a lysate is not a surface-only survey, and in multi-allele samples a peptide was assigned to the best-scoring allele or alleles by computation (Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020). Identification depends on the analysis: a deep-learning model trained on more than 300,000 synthetic peptides improved HLA peptide identification up to 7-fold and indicated that 87 per cent of the proposed proteasomally spliced HLA peptides may be incorrect (Wilhelm and colleagues, 2021). A quantitative tissue study isolated peptide-HLA complexes from snap-frozen tissue and used formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded blocks only for histology (Science Translational Medicine, 2022).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). In a mixed specimen a recovered HLA-associated peptide does not reveal its cell of origin or its abundance on living cell surfaces. Non-detection does not show biological absence: it also reflects capture, allele coverage, the searchable sequence set and instrument and software sensitivity, and detection does not show safe tumour recognition. No source read here establishes that formalin-fixed tissue is usable for an assay validated on cells or frozen tissue; the lesson's statement that one protocol proposed an adaptation could not be checked (publisher page unavailable), so that claim is withheld and compatibility must be shown for the named method.

Fictional worked example. A specimen yields peptide A but not peptide B. A has measured support in that preparation. For B, ask whether its allele was recovered, whether the altered sequence was searchable and whether sensitivity was adequate; 'A detected, B absent everywhere' is stronger than the experiment supports. If B is simply missing from the search database it could not have been identified as configured, so its absence is not a clean biological negative, and correcting the database does not by itself guarantee recovery or prove natural display.

Reading guide: binding prediction estimates a model output, whereas immunopeptidomics identifies recovered peptides, and total-protein measurements are a different question from HLA-associated fragments (a protein can be abundant without any of its peptides being displayed, an inference); presentation, immune response and efficacy are three separate claims.

Measurement card in words (a reading guide). Input: which tissue preparation and preservation are compatible, and how much material is consumed. Output and units: peptide identities and unique-sequence counts; instrument intensities are method-dependent and not copies per cell. Identification threshold: the sequence database, the false-discovery rule (spectrum or peptide level) and the supporting spectra. Coverage: which HLA classes and alleles were captured and which allele assignments were measured or inferred. Material and cost: protocol-specific input, preservation, consumption, turnaround and analysis cost, requested before a scarce specimen is used. Validation: recovery, reproducibility and reference-peptide checks for the method. Failure modes: low input, poor recovery, mixed cell populations, database gaps and wrong sequence assignments. Limits: non-detection does not prove absence and detection does not prove safe recognition; there is no universal tissue requirement or detection threshold.

records.name: Peptide-HLA binding and ligand prediction
records.tldr: A computer model can prioritize peptides expected to bind an immune display molecule or appear among its ligands. The prediction helps select candidates for testing.
records.summary: NetMHCpan-4.0 combined peptide-binding affinity data with eluted-ligand data, which also contain information about processing and natural presentation. Those training signals and prediction tasks should be distinguished. A consortium comparison assessed candidate tumor epitopes using measured immune interactions and developed improved prioritization features. A model score is a prediction with a validation setting; it is not an observation of peptide display, tumor recognition or patient benefit. The NetMHCpan-4.1 documentation expresses binder thresholds as percentile rank, the position of a predicted score against the scores of random natural peptides, and lets the user set the strong and weak binder thresholds, so a 0.4 per cent rank places a candidate within the top 0.4 per cent of that reference and is not a 99.6 per cent probability of presentation, recognition or benefit. The server predicts binding of a peptide to an MHC molecule of known sequence, and its model is trained on more than 850,000 binding-affinity and mass-spectrometry eluted-ligand peptides, two different training signals (Reynisson and colleagues, 2020). A model trained on more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 single-allele cell lines improved prediction of presented peptides (Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020). In a consortium study, 608 predicted epitopes were then tested for T-cell binding in patient-matched samples, a separate experiment from the prediction (Wells and colleagues, 2020), so expression, processing, display, T-cell receptor recognition and sparing of healthy tissue remain to be shown after a favourable score.

notes: Assay distinction. A predicted binding IC50 estimates a competitive-binding assay endpoint. An IC50 depends on the assay conditions and is not automatically an equilibrium dissociation constant. Cer and colleagues' 2009 IC50-to-Ki tool calculates binding or inhibition constants using the interaction mechanism, concentrations and other assumptions; this is a biochemical distinction, not validation of an HLA model or a measure of cancer-cell growth inhibition. Reading guide (OnCo inference): Record the model and version, allele, peptide length, prediction task, units, reference distribution and threshold beside every score, and do not put a rank and an IC50 in one unlabelled column. A threshold is a selection rule for a stated workflow and cannot repair the wrong allele or an unsupported task. Inputs are peptide or source-protein sequences and an exact allele; scoring uses no tumour tissue; held-out validation, allele coverage and the endpoint (binding, recovery or T-cell recognition) decide what a good score means.

Figure reading (fictional numbers, light and dark renders agree): a 1,000-score reference for HLA-A*02:01 9-mer peptides has bin counts 250, 240, 200, 130, 80, 50, 30, 16 and 4, which sum to 1,000. Four reference scores lie beyond the candidate boundary, so 4 / 1,000 x 100 = 0.4 per cent. A separate binding-affinity output of 40 nM is a predicted IC50. Neither value observes display.

Fictional worked example. Candidate A has an eluted-ligand rank of 0.4 per cent and candidate B a predicted binding IC50 of 40 nM. The numbers come from different outputs with different units and tasks, so neither ranks the candidates against each other or shows tumour coverage; request matched outputs for the relevant allele and method, and test display and recognition separately.

Output table in words. Predicted binding IC50 in nanomolar units: lower values mean stronger predicted competitive binding for that output, and it is not a measured concentration, an equilibrium dissociation constant or a functional T-cell response. Percentile rank: a lower rank places the candidate nearer the model's stronger-scoring reference peptides, and it is not a percent chance of tumour killing or the fraction of tumour cells covered.

records.name: Immunodominance
records.tldr: Immune responses to a set of possible targets are often uneven. Some epitopes attract a stronger measured response than others in the same setting.
records.summary: A primary mouse experiment showed that T-cell populations could compete for access to antigen-bearing presenting cells, changing responses to dominant and subdominant epitopes. That identifies one mechanism of immunodominance in the studied system. It does not supply a universal ranking of human tumor epitopes. The antigen design, presentation context and responding repertoire all need to remain attached to an observation of a dominant response.

notes: Immunodominance is a contextual hierarchy of measured responses, distinct from encoded target count and from epitope spreading. Presentation, precursor frequency, repertoire, priming, HLA, delivery, immune history, tissue and time can change the hierarchy. A favourable binding prediction does not establish immunogenicity, and more encoded targets do not guarantee balanced immunity or independent tumour coverage.

Naive precursor frequency is the starting abundance of cells with a relevant specificity. Mouse LCMV and human HLA-A2-restricted HCV experiments linked precursor frequencies to response hierarchies. Binding alone did not strictly predict the hierarchy. These studies provide no universal cancer-vaccine weights, human marker requirement or instruction to remove dominant clones.

Fictional matched IFN-gamma ELISpot means of 45, 11 and 5 spots for A, B and C, minus matched background 5, give 40, 6 and 0 spots per 200,000 plated PBMCs. A dominates that measured response. Protocol replicate and positivity rules classify C as undetectable. Zero adjusted spots do not prove absent tumour display or universal uselessness, nor do three encoded sequences imply three equally effective responses.

A measured hierarchy needs offered targets, compartment, cell denominator, baseline, timing, matched per-target stimulation, background and positive controls. Detection thresholds and in vitro expansion can alter apparent ranking. Peptide response is not evidence of natural tumour display or tumour-cell killing.

records.name: Epitope spreading
records.tldr: An immune response can broaden to recognize additional epitopes over time. Showing that broadening requires measurements of the added specificities.
records.summary: A follow-up study of a small melanoma neoantigen-vaccine cohort found persistent immune responses, evolving receptor clonotypes and evidence of responses beyond the original vaccine targets. The report provides clinical immune-monitoring evidence of spreading in that cohort. The response measurements are distinct from a randomized estimate of treatment benefit. Spreading should not be inferred solely from an increased total lymphocyte count or expansion of an unidentified receptor sequence.

notes: Epitope spreading is additional detected recognition beyond the initially targeted epitope set, potentially within one source protein or across proteins. More response to the same target is expansion. Responses to both directly encoded A and B do not themselves demonstrate spreading. Newly detected is not newly created: baseline sensitivity can miss pre-existing responsive cells.

Tumour injury can release additional antigen for uptake and presentation, but one follow-up response does not establish that entire causal chain. Define peptide-HLA targets and compare matched baseline and follow-up assays with background, presentation and cross-reactivity controls; assess intervening treatment. Vaccine recruitment or expansion does not normally rewrite mature TCRs. An immune response, including one to healthy self, does not establish recurrence prevention, safety or clinical benefit.

In a fictional A/B vaccine experiment, baseline C is undetectable and matched follow-up detects unencoded C, consistent with an additional detected specificity. The A-cell icons are qualitative, not counts. records.name: Messenger RNA construct anatomy
aka: mRNA untranslated regions and poly(A) tail
records.tldr: An engineered messenger RNA includes a protein-coding message and surrounding features that affect how it is used. Those features are part of the construct being tested.
records.summary:
The cap, untranslated regions, coding sequence and poly(A) tail are distinct parts of a messenger RNA construct. A primary dendritic-cell study changed untranslated-region and poly(A)-tail features and measured RNA stability, protein production, peptide display and T-cell stimulation separately. Another experimental study separated effects of codon usage and RNA structure on protein expression. Construct design therefore includes more than the intended amino-acid sequence. A design that improves one measured step in one system does not establish optimal immune effects or clinical efficacy in another.

Start-codon context was tested by single-base substitutions around the AUG initiator in a cloned preproinsulin gene, where the best sequence identified changed proinsulin yield over a 20-fold range (Kozak). The interaction of the cap and the poly(A) tail was tested with luciferase mRNAs delivered by electroporation into tobacco protoplasts, Chinese hamster ovary cells and yeast, where the tail's effect depended on the cap (Gallie). A textbook describes the 5' cap, 5' and 3' untranslated regions that regulate translation initiation and mRNA stability, a poly-A tail of about 200 A residues added by poly-A polymerase to cellular mRNA, and a ribosome that moves from the cap to the AUG, with Kozak's rules describing the sequence around it (OpenStax Biology 2e). The cellular tail length is not a rule for engineered constructs: one dendritic-cell study found that a 120-nucleotide tail, an unmasked tail end and two 3' untranslated regions each improved stability and translation, and it measured transcript amount by RT-PCR, protein by eGFP, peptide-MHC density and T-cell stimulation separately (Holtkamp and colleagues), so a doubled reporter signal after a 3' change is one measurement, not a different antigen or a clinical benefit. These are tested constructs and cell systems, not one best sequence for a clinical product.

records.summary:

Work on engineered messenger RNAs also separated codon usage from RNA secondary structure, showing that expression depends on more than a simple codon preference. Optimization is a design objective with a particular assay and system, not a guarantee of improved therapy. Changing codons is distinct from choosing which antigen or epitope the construct encodes.

In four human cell lines, three independent methods showed that mRNA stability tracked codon identity rather than nucleotide content, stabilising codons tended to coincide with higher tRNA levels, and the effect depended on translation (Wu and colleagues, 2019). Another study separated codon usage from coding-region structure in eGFP constructs and defined functional half-life as the time an mRNA is actively translated, which differs from RNA that is merely present or protein that persists, so a doubled reporter signal at one time point does not show twice the RNA lifetime, a better neoantigen or any clinical effect (Mauger and colleagues).

records.name: Modified nucleosides in messenger RNA
records.tldr: Chemical changes to RNA building blocks can alter how a message is sensed and translated. The effect depends on the RNA and the system in which it is tested.
records.summary:
Primary experiments found that selected nucleoside modifications changed RNA-triggered innate immune activation. Later work showed that purification of modified transcripts also affected inflammatory responses and protein expression. Modification and removal of contaminants are therefore distinct design and manufacturing questions. Results from those experimental systems do not establish that one modification is best for every cancer vaccine, delivery platform or intended immune response.

In cell lines and mice, N1-methylpseudouridine, alone or with 5-methylcytidine, gave higher reporter expression than pseudouridine-based mRNA, up to about 44-fold for double-modified mRNA and about 13-fold for single-modified mRNA as the abstract reports (cell lines and mice respectively), with less innate immunogenicity and better cell viability in vitro (Andries and colleagues). Separately, N1-methylpseudouridine caused +1 ribosomal frameshifting in vitro at slippery sequences, cellular immunity to +1 products was found in mice and humans after vaccination with BNT162b2 vaccine mRNA, and synonymous changes at those sequences reduced frameshifted products; the authors note that no adverse outcomes from mistranslation of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have been reported (Mulroney and colleagues). More reporter signal with less cytokine in one matched comparison does not show a stronger antigen-specific T-cell response: unmodified mRNAs were translated better after purification yet still induced high cytokine secretion, and purified modified mRNA was translated 10 to 1000-fold more in primary cells (Karikó and colleagues, 2011), so sensing, expression and T-cell readouts each need their own evidence.

records.name: In vitro transcription for RNA products
records.tldr: Enzymes can copy a DNA template into RNA outside a living cell. Producing the transcript is followed by questions about its identity, composition and suitability for use.
records.summary:
Experimental RNA-manufacturing studies distinguish the intended in vitro-transcribed RNA from contaminating products and test how purification affects its performance. A primary RNA-construct study then measured expression and immune stimulation after delivering transcripts to cells. RNA production, product quality and biological performance are separate observations. An RNA yield or a band of the expected size alone does not establish a released product or a clinical treatment effect.

A protocol from authors affiliated with TriLink Biotechnologies describes co-transcriptional capping with the company's CleanCap AG reagent, reported to give 94 per cent cap 1 structure at 5 mg/ml of transcription, against cap 0 products at lower efficiency from first-generation cap analogues (Henderson and colleagues). Separately, T7 polymerase initiated transcription from a promoter-less DNA end and made an antisense strand that paired with the intended RNA as long double-stranded RNA, which stimulated the innate sensor MDA5; the activity was suppressed by modified nucleotides or a lower magnesium concentration (Mu and colleagues). Release analytics are layered: reviews list sequence and modification identity, poly(A) tail, RNA content by UV spectrophotometry, integrity and transcript length by gel or capillary electrophoresis or chromatography, double-stranded RNA by immunoblot or ELISA, and residual DNA as separate attributes; purification has to remove template DNA, unincorporated nucleotides and enzymes; residual nucleotides are controlled below predefined thresholds that need much lower detection limits than the main product, with the intact mRNA itself complicating their detection (Losada and colleagues; Nowak and colleagues). records.name: Double-stranded RNA impurities
records.tldr: RNA manufacture can also produce unwanted paired RNA material. Measuring and removing it is a product-quality question separate from the intended message.
records.summary:
Primary experiments identified double-stranded RNA among contaminants that affected innate immune activation and translation of in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA. Subsequent work developed and tested a cellulose-based removal method. Those studies support characterizing contaminants and their functional consequences in the tested workflows. They do not establish one universal acceptable impurity level or release method for all RNA products.

One documented origin is T7 polymerase initiating transcription from a promoter-less DNA end, producing an antisense strand and long double-stranded RNA that activated the sensor MDA5 (Mu and colleagues). In purification studies, unmodified mRNAs were translated better after HPLC purification but still induced high levels of cytokine secretion (Karikó and colleagues). A cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery regardless of mRNA length, coding sequence or nucleoside composition and increased translation in mice, and agarose gels showed that the purified mRNA stayed intact, but it removed duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer efficiently while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Detection has its own scope: that paper notes an earlier report that about 40 base pairs of duplex are needed for detection by the J2 antibody, and a review of mRNA analytics lists immunoblot or ELISA for double-stranded RNA alongside separate integrity assays (Losada and colleagues). A lower dsRNA signal with worse fragmentation or recovery therefore does not show a better product. Method performance in those systems is not a clinical impurity limit.

records.name: Multi-epitope constructs and antigen processing
records.tldr: A construct can encode several intended immune targets. Each target still needs to be processed, displayed and recognized in the tested biological setting.
records.summary:
A primary multiepitope DNA-vaccine study found that flanking sequence changes altered processing efficiency and measured immunogenicity of encoded epitopes. That was evidence from the tested constructs, not a validated rule for every RNA cancer vaccine. The number of encoded epitopes is distinct from the number naturally displayed or recognized. Processing evidence, immune-response breadth and clinical outcome remain separate parts of a construct claim.

A computational study of spacer design for class-I-restricted string-of-beads polypeptides reported a fivefold increase in predicted epitope recovery and a 44 per cent reduction in predicted neo-epitope immunogenicity compared with designs without spacers (Schubert and Kohlbacher); these are predictions, not measured protection. Combining an N-terminal leader peptide with an MHC class I trafficking signal at the C terminus improved presentation of class I and class II epitopes in human and mouse dendritic cells and expanded antigen-specific CD8 and CD4 T cells in vitro and in mice (Kreiter and colleagues). In a first-in-human RNA poly-neo-epitope melanoma study all patients developed T-cell responses against multiple vaccine neo-epitopes (Sahin and colleagues; abstract only), and each patient's vaccine in the Rojas pancreatic cancer trial used two uridine mRNA strands, each encoding up to 10 neoepitopes. Mass spectrometry can identify recovered HLA-bound peptides. Caron and colleagues' 2015 review describes class I peptides predominantly 9 to 12 amino acids long and reports that about 10 per cent of acquired spectra could be confidently assigned at a 1 per cent false discovery rate in the workflows discussed. It also describes evidence that mass spectrometry underestimates the self-HLA peptide repertoire, so non-detection does not prove absence. Prediction is not presentation: of more than 1,300 amino acid changes in two mouse tumour models about 13 per cent were predicted to bind MHC class I and a small fraction of those were confirmed by mass spectrometry (Yadav and colleagues). Because a single amino acid after an epitope changed its immunogenicity in a multiepitope DNA vaccine (Livingston and colleagues, already linked), a changed spacer is a changed construct that needs renewed processing and display evidence, while earlier evidence is retained for the parts that did not change.

records.tldr: The molecule used to deliver an intervention to a cell can differ from the target of the treatment that cell produces. Both targeting steps need to be named.
records.summary:
A primary mouse cardiac-fibrosis study used CD5-targeted lipid nanoparticles to deliver RNA encoding a receptor directed against fibroblast activation protein. CD5 specified a delivery interaction; the encoded receptor had a different recognition target. This is a non-oncology preclinical illustration of the distinction, not cancer-treatment evidence. Delivery, expression, effector recognition and clinical benefit should retain their separate experiments and biological settings.

Targeted-LNP studies show three separate questions. Which cells receive usable cargo: in the CD5 study mRNA reached most cultured mouse T cells (83 per cent expressed the receptor, against 7 per cent with isotype-control particles) and receptor expression appeared across the main T-cell subsets in injured mice, while liver expression occurred with both CD5 and control particles; recombination in a Cre reporter reached 81.1 per cent of CD4-positive and 75.6 per cent of CD8-positive splenocytes but also 15.0 per cent of CD3-negative cells, and the statement that 87 per cent of receptor-positive cells were CD4-positive is a share of expressing cells, not the share of CD4 T cells that expressed the receptor, so each percentage needs its denominator. What the receptor recognises: FDA's January 2024 CAR T guidance says cytokine release and killing should be antigen-dependent, testable with cells that vary in target antigen expression, and asks sponsors to assess targeting of healthy tissue that expresses the intended antigen (on-target, off-tumour) and of other antigens (off-target); activity against antigen-positive healthy cells would therefore show target-dependent activity and a safety concern, not selective cancer killing. Where engineered cells act is a further question: a later study with targeted lipid nanoparticles reports reprogrammed CD8-positive T cells from healthy donors and autoimmune patients, tumour control in humanised mice and B-cell depletion in cynomolgus monkeys, each a different experiment and setting (Hunter and colleagues; abstract only). For a vaccine the address can instead be an antigen-presenting cell: intravenous RNA-lipoplexes were aimed at dendritic cells and macrophages in lymphoid compartments by adjusting net charge, without a molecular ligand (Kranz and colleagues).

records.name: Cell segmentation in tissue measurements
records.tldr: Image analysis estimates which pixels or detected molecules belong to each cell. Those assignments affect the measurements reported for that cell.
records.summary: The Mesmer study developed and tested whole-cell segmentation across tissue images and used the estimated boundaries to extract cellular features. A separate spatial-transcriptomics reanalysis found that misassigned molecules could change downstream cell-state and interaction analyses. These findings concern defined datasets and methods, not one universal error rate. Segmentation quality and signal assignment need evaluation before a spatial measurement is treated as a biological conclusion. Mesmer was trained on TissueNet, a dataset of more than 1 million manually labelled cells, and was reported to generalise across the tissue types and imaging platforms in that dataset at human-level performance; its authors note that segmentation inaccuracies can substantially bias the identification and counting of cells, and that cells whose nucleus lies outside the imaging plane are missed by nucleus-based methods (Greenwald and colleagues, 2022). In that evaluation, a predicted and a true cell with a one-to-one match by intersection over union count as accurate, predicted cells with no match are false positives and true cells with no match are false negatives. The Cellpose study reported a generalist method trained on more than 70,000 segmented objects that worked without retraining across the image types it evaluated (Stringer and colleagues, 2021). Baysor was developed because methods that approximate cell positions from nuclear stains make cell boundaries hard to distinguish in single-molecule spatial data (Petukhov and colleagues, 2022).

notes: Reading guide (definitions plus OnCo inference). Detection asks whether a cell was found, segmentation asks which pixels belong to it, and phenotyping classifies the cell afterwards; finding a nucleus does not give a reliable whole-cell boundary. Intersection over union is the area two masks share divided by the area either covers, from 0 to 1, and a single value can hide missed or merged cells, so check object counts and characteristic errors too. A mask assigns existing signals to estimated regions and is not a measurement of a new marker. Merging, splitting and missing cells distort counts, marker combinations and spatial relations, so overlay masks on the original channels.

Fictional worked example (two stipulated cells). One mask covers a small T cell and an adjacent cancer cell, so one table row reports both an immune marker and keratin; that is a merged object, not a hybrid cell. A split into three objects for two cells adds objects, not cells. Correcting the mask may show two neighbouring cells, and their proximity still does not prove immune recognition.

Figure reading (synthetic, light and dark renders agree): the marker channels A (immune) and K (keratin) stay fixed while a merged mask gives one object, a split gives three, and a shifted border assigns signals to the wrong object; the table changes and the image does not. An overlay does not prove identity or function.

Analysis card in words (a reading guide). Input and tissue cost: existing image channels and scale information; computation consumes no additional tissue, though upstream staining or imaging may already have consumed material. Output and units: labelled masks, object counts, estimated cell area in square micrometres when calibrated, coordinates and distances in micrometres, and unitless overlap scores. Controls: original-image overlays, representative manual annotations, held-out images, checks by cell type and region, and recorded software, model and settings. Thresholds: error tolerances set for the downstream task. Failure modes: merged, split or missing cells, weak boundary stains, misaligned channels, debris, and tissue or stain differences from the development data. Cannot tell you: new molecular signals, complete cell outlines outside the section, receptor specificity, interaction or killing. Validation context: an image-analysis component validated for a defined tissue, acquisition and task.

records.name: Targeted proteomics and quantification limits
records.tldr: A targeted protein assay measures selected peptide signals through a defined workflow. Reliable amounts require evidence about the quantitative range and precision of the assay.
records.summary: A primary multilaboratory study evaluated isotope-dilution multiple-reaction-monitoring assays for selected plasma proteins, examining recovery, reproducibility, linear range, detection and quantification limits. The performance belonged to the tested materials, analytes and protocols. It was not a universal certificate for all proteins or specimens. A reported protein amount should retain its measured peptide, calibration approach, sample preparation and supported range. An NIH workshop report on targeted mass spectrometry found no consensus on the criteria for a successful peptide assay and set out three tiers of assay performance, with response and calibration curves generated for each analyte in the relevant matrix to establish limits of detection and quantification; quantification rests on precursor-product ion pairs, called transitions, shown to be free of interference, and a surrogate protein standard must be shown to behave like the native analyte in tests of recovery after adding a known amount (Carr and colleagues, 2014). Stable-isotope-labelled internal standard peptides with the sequence of the analyte are spiked into the digest, and extended peptides or recombinant proteins can compensate for variability in digestion (Hoofnagle and colleagues, 2016). A multilaboratory plasma study reported reproducibility, recovery, linear range and limits of detection and quantification at microgram-per-millilitre protein concentrations (Addona and colleagues, 2009).

Hoofnagle et al., Recommendations for the Generation, Quantification, Storage, and Handling of Peptides Used for Mass Spectrometry-Based Assays (Clinical Chemistry 2016)

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference built on the ICH definitions). A signal detected below the quantification limit is meaningful as detection, but it does not support a reliable amount, and neither it nor non-detection means biological zero. An upper limit also bounds the range, and a saturated response cannot separate larger inputs. Keep the denominator with every amount (for example femtomoles per microgram of total extracted protein or a concentration per volume), because it describes the mixture and not receptors per malignant cell; a selected peptide is a proxy for its source protein and cannot count intact receptors or surface copies. Tight repeats show precision, which can coexist with systematic bias. A standard added after digestion can control later measurement but cannot correct material already lost.

Fictional worked example. A summary says 'receptor peptide R is absent' for an assay that detected R below its quantification limit. The result should read 'detected below the validated quantification limit', with the limit and units: it supports detection under that assay's rules but neither a dependable amount nor biological absence.

Figure reading (fictional calibration, light and dark renders agree, no cutoff): a calibration plot has four regions in order of rising input, blank or background (no detection claim), detected below the lower limit of quantification (no reliable amount), validated range (report amount and units) and upper saturation (the response flattens), with replicate points scattered on the curve; a second panel says peptide amount is not surface location, and tight repeats alone do not rule out bias. Limits belong to the analyte and matrix.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Measures and how: selected peptide amounts, by extracting, digesting, measuring specified ions and fragments with controls, calibrating and assessing analyte performance. Input and tissue cost: a validated tissue, cell or fluid matrix; extraction and digestion consume material, and required mass or volume and fixation compatibility are assay-specific. Output and units: peptide identity, amount or ratio, with the denominator and the peptide-to-protein inference kept. Thresholds: analyte-specific limit of detection, quantification limit, upper limit, bias and precision acceptance and reportable range, with no universal limit or treatment threshold. Failure modes: incomplete recovery or digestion, shared peptides, interference, unstable standards, matrix effects and signal outside the validated range. Limits: no automatic intact-form, location, cell-of-origin, accessibility, occupancy or drug-dependence conclusion. Validation tier: fit-for-purpose research tiers describe analytical characterisation and do not themselves confer clinical approval.

records.name: Antigen presentation & immune editing
records.tldr: Cells display protein fragments that immune cells can recognize. Tumors can escape by changing this display or suppressing immune responses. Recognition and target-cell killing are separate steps.
records.summary: Proteasome-processed peptides are loaded on MHC class I (HLA-A/B/C, B2M) and presented to CD8 T cells; dendritic cells cross-present tumour antigens in lymph nodes. Immunoediting proceeds through elimination, equilibrium, and escape: loss of B2M or HLA, JAK1/2 or IFNGR mutations (blunting interferon-γ response), antigen loss, PD-L1 induction, and immunosuppressive niches. Candidate epitope selection considers presentation and immune recognition; these require evidence beyond mutation count or predicted binding. HLA genotype shapes which peptides can be displayed. Escape variants explain acquired resistance to checkpoint blockade and CAR-T (CD19 loss).

records.name: Cell-therapy release and potency testing
records.tldr: A cell-product lot is checked against specified quality requirements before its disposition. Identity, live-cell measures and biological activity answer different questions about that lot.
records.summary: FDA's final potency-assurance guidance describes a product-specific strategy spanning manufacturing design, controls, materials, in-process testing and lot-release assays. CAR T-cell guidance separately discusses safety, identity, quality, purity and potency measurements. A viability result or marker-expression result is not automatically equivalent to a functional bioassay. Assay choice and acceptance criteria depend on the product and development context. Passing a release specification is distinct from estimating clinical benefit in a patient.

notes: FDA's November 2026 final potency-assurance guidance supersedes its January 2011 potency-tests guidance. Its scope is cellular and gene therapy biological products regulated under section 351 of the U.S. Public Health Service Act. Potency assurance includes process and material controls, in-process evidence, release assays, stability and in-use handling; a release assay alone does not establish the clinical benefit of a particular lot.

For CAR T cells, FDA's 2024 guidance recommends identity evidence for the transgene and intended cellular composition. HLA typing alone does not detect the genetic modification or replace chain-of-identity records. Biological identity and the association with the intended recipient are separate checks.

For an integrating-vector CAR T-cell product, the 2024 guidance describes average vector copy number per CAR-positive cell on the lot certificate of analysis. Including CAR-negative cells in the denominator can understate the value in the modified population. The average does not show insertion locations or clonal distribution. Short processes can retain non-integrated vector copies, so a release measurement may need a later assessment in cultured cells to determine stable integration; the interval is product-specific.

Replication-competent virus testing, microbial sterility, mycoplasma, endotoxin and engineered-cell identity address different hazards or attributes. The applicable tests, methods and acceptance criteria depend on the product, process and development stage. Detecting a sequence or a receptor does not demonstrate every intended biological activity.

For ex vivo genetically modified cells administered immediately after manufacture, FDA's 2020 gene-therapy CMC guidance describes an in-process sterility sample taken 48 to 72 hours before final harvest plus a rapid test such as a Gram stain on final product. Under that approach, negative Gram stain and no growth in the in-process test can support release while the final-product culture continues for its full duration, for example 14 days for USP <71>. The guidance calls for a plan addressing a later positive result, clinical management, investigation and reporting to the investigator and FDA. These are scoped recommendations, not universal early-release criteria for every cell product.

FDA's CAR T-cell examples distinguish activity against each target in a multi-antigen product, production of an added cytokine and a drug-resistance function. Each relevant transgene activity may need suitable evidence. A single expression or cell-count result is not the complete functional package.

In a fictional 100-cell teaching sample, 80 cells are live and 60 of those live cells express the receptor. Viability is 80/100, receptor positivity among live cells is 60/80, and live receptor-positive cells among all counted cells are 60/100. Receptor status of the nonlive cells is unspecified. These different denominators establish neither potency nor a clinical release cutoff.
records.principle: Product-specific control strategies combine defined quality attributes, suitable assays and justified acceptance criteria; a release result retains its lot and intended use.
limitations: Testing and sample availability can constrain release
Relationship to clinical outcomes needs product-specific evidence
Sampling uses a portion of the lot

The NCI Biospecimen Preanalytical Variables program examined delay and duration effects in defined tumor specimens and found that quality assays differed in what they detected. NCI best practices therefore emphasize documented collection, processing and tracking. A protocol or numerical limit appropriate to one assay should not be treated as a universal rule for every tissue, analyte or downstream test.

records.name: Flow cytometry (immunophenotyping)
records.tldr: A test that measures light signals from individual cells or particles. Stained markers can identify cell types, and specialized assays can examine what those cells are doing.
records.summary: Flow cytometry measures features of prepared cells as they pass through an instrument. Immunophenotyping uses combinations of markers to distinguish cell populations, including in blood-cancer diagnosis and residual-disease testing. Other methods measure intracellular cytokines, degranulation or target-cell death. Primary method studies show that these are different readouts, and validation depends on preparation, panel, controls and analysis gates. The performance of one assay does not automatically validate every use of the platform.

records.name: Vein-to-vein time and manufacturing slots
records.tldr: Vein-to-vein time measures the interval from collecting a person's cells to infusing the manufactured cell product. Shipping, manufacturing, quality testing and clinical scheduling can all contribute to the wait.
records.summary: The interval follows a patient-specific product through collection, manufacture, testing, transport and administration. Manufacturing outcome, lot quality and eventual infusion are separate observations. A UK retrospective CAR T-cell report used manufacturing failure as an umbrella covering both no product and an out-of-specification product, with some patients subsequently receiving a remanufactured or specially assessed lot. Published rates therefore need their study definitions; they do not directly state the chance that an individual will receive treatment.

notes: Chain of identity links material and product to the source and intended recipient. Chain-of-custody records describe movement, handoffs and handling. FDA CAR T-cell guidance addresses identity tracking; NCI biospecimen guidance describes custody records in its own specimen-management scope.

An out-of-specification lot does not meet at least one specified criterion. Its existence does not establish that it is suitable or authorized for infusion; disposition is a product- and situation-specific question.

A timing estimate needs its exact start and end events. Collection-to-infusion, order-to-infusion, enrolment-to-infusion, receipt-to-release and culture duration are different clocks. State elapsed calendar days, the cohort, handling of repeat collections and the spread, rather than assigning one turnaround to every product.

In a fictional workflow, collection is day 0, culture ends on day 7, release is day 12 and infusion is day 18. Collection-to-infusion time is 18 days; the stated culture interval is seven days. These teaching numbers are not a scheduling promise.

A median calculated among infused people cannot assign an infusion time to people who never received cells. Report how many entered the stated pathway, how many reached infusion, the follow-up window and reasons for non-infusion separately. Manufacturing, conformity, shipment and patient readiness need their own denominators and event definitions.

FDA's 2024 CAR T-cell guidance discusses disease progression and changing eligibility during manufacturing, product availability before a high-risk lymphodepleting regimen, and contingency plans for failure to treat. Bridging therapy can also confound response attribution; the guidance recommends appropriate disease reassessment and prespecified analyses that retain bridging-treatment context. This is clinical-study guidance, not a universal bridging or scheduling rule.

records.name: Reverse-phase protein array (RPPA)
records.tldr: This array tests protein extracts from many samples using selected antibodies. The panel and its validation determine which protein signals can be interpreted.
records.summary: A reverse-phase protein array places sample lysates on an array and measures selected proteins or modifications with antibodies. The original tissue study examined signaling proteins in defined cell populations. A later study used phosphatase treatment as an independent control when characterizing phospho-antibodies for frozen and fixed tissue. Signal specificity, input preparation and validation matter. A lysate measurement does not restore the spatial arrangement lost during extraction, and phosphorylation signal needs interpretation alongside protein abundance. In the original reverse-phase protein microarray, the whole repertoire of a patient's tissue proteins from laser-capture microdissected cell populations is immobilised and probed, in contrast to earlier arrays that immobilise the probe, and precision and linearity were tested with microarrayed dilution curves of a standard protein and loading was normalised with an actin control (Paweletz and colleagues, 2001). Because target detection relies on a single antibody, RNA interference was used to test antibody performance: two anti-EGFR antibodies detected knockdown at different rates, and four of ten anti-STAT3 antibodies detected STAT3 knockdown at 80 to 85 per cent (Mannsperger and colleagues, 2010). Ischaemia changed phosphorylation in human ovarian tumour tissue and breast cancer xenografts, which supports recording how tissue was collected and preserved without setting a universal safe delay (Mertins and colleagues, 2014).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). A printed spot holds a mixed lysate, and its address names a sample and a dilution, not a cell position in tissue. Dilution curves, background, references and loading normalisation define the usable range, and signals from two antibodies are not on the same scale. A phosphosite signal is not occupancy or enzymatic activity, because it can reflect more source protein, a larger modified fraction or preparation effects.

Fictional worked example. A phospho-R signal doubles, but total R and loading were not evaluated. The report cannot call this doubled R activity: check loading, source-protein abundance, antibody performance, handling and the site's function, since the observed increase is narrower than an activity claim.

Figure reading (toy dilutions, light and dark renders agree): cells are disrupted into one mixed lysate, so location is lost; samples A and B are printed at dilutions 1, 1/2 and 1/4, giving six addresses, and each spot is still a mixture; separate replicate arrays are probed for R and for phospho-R. Each antibody and signal scale needs validation, and this is neither an all-protein census nor a single-cell map.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Measures and how: selected antibody-recognised epitopes, by extracting lysate, printing dilutions, probing replicate arrays, quantifying signal and normalising with controls. Input and tissue cost: an assay-compatible lysate; extraction consumes material and destroys arrangement, and microdissection defines the sampled region without keeping coordinates inside the lysate. Output and units: antibody and epitope identifiers with relative or normalised signal; calibrated amounts only when specifically supported. Thresholds: antibody-specific validated range, dilution behaviour, background and report criteria, with no universal activation or treatment cutoff. Failure modes: cross-reactivity, loading differences, saturated or weak signal, cell mixture, handling-induced modification change and batch effects. Limits: no automatic intact-form, spatial map, whole-pathway activity, cell-specific surface amount, dependency or benefit conclusion. Validation tier: primarily a research profiling method.
